This vignette describes how to run the complete global analysis on the UBELIX
Slurm cluster. Commands are intended to be run from the top-level
`mct_limitations` directory. The workflow uses daily MSWEP V3.16 Past total
precipitation, ERA5-Land temperature, and ALEXI evapotranspiration under the
default configuration.

The submission helpers create Slurm arrays, request the resources recorded in
`src/ubelix/jobs.tsv`, add the configured climate-source tag to job and output
names, and retain completed longitude checkpoints when a job is restarted.

## 1. Prepare the project and R environment

Log in to UBELIX, enter the project checkout, and confirm that the project file
is present. Always submit from this directory because Slurm records it as the
job's working directory.

```{bash}
cd /path/to/mct_limitations
test -f mct.Rproj
git status --short
```

Load R and install the dependencies once into an R library available on the
compute nodes. The `remotes` installer reads `DESCRIPTION`, including the
GitHub packages listed under `Remotes`.

```{bash}
module load R
Rscript -e 'if (!requireNamespace("remotes", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("remotes", repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")'
Rscript -e 'remotes::install_deps(dependencies = TRUE)'
```

If packages are centrally managed or already installed, only verify that the
project loads the key dependencies.

```{bash}
Rscript -e 'library(cwd); library(map2tidy); library(rgeco)'
```

## 2. Configure and verify the climate inputs

Review `config/input_sources.R` before submitting. In particular, verify the
analysis years, NetCDF directories and filename patterns, variable and
coordinate names, source grids, and the elevation file. Paths beginning with
`~` are expanded on the compute node and must therefore resolve there.

The default run identifier can be printed without starting a calculation.

```{bash}
Rscript -e 'source("R/input_config.R"); config <- read_input_config(); cat(climate_run_id(config), "\n")'
```

For a different namelist, export `MCT_INPUT_CONFIG` before every status or
submission command. Slurm exports this variable to the compute jobs.

```{bash}
export MCT_INPUT_CONFIG=config/input_sources_alternative.R
Rscript -e 'source("R/input_config.R"); config <- read_input_config(); cat(climate_run_id(config), "\n")'
```

Run the status report before submission. A new run should mostly report zero
outputs; an interrupted or completed run will show the tagged checkpoints that
already exist.

```{bash}
Rscript analysis/00_status.R
```

## 3. Workflow jobs and dependencies

The retained workflow consists of these jobs:

| Order | Job name | Requires | Main purpose |
|---:|---|---|---|
| 1 | `prepare_precipitation` | MSWEP NetCDF files | Create tidy precipitation longitude slices |
| 1 | `prepare_temperature` | ERA5-Land NetCDF files | Create tidy temperature longitude slices |
| 1 | `prepare_et` | ALEXI NetCDF files | Create tidy ET longitude slices |
| 2 | `convert_et_mm` | tidy ET and temperature | Convert ALEXI latent energy to daily ET in mm |
| 2 | `simulate_snow` | tidy precipitation and temperature | Partition rain and snow, maintain snow storage, and calculate melt |
| 3 | `calculate_balance` | converted ET and liquid input | Calculate daily rain plus snowmelt minus ET |
| 4 | `calculate_annual_cwd` | daily balance | Store annual maximum CWD and preceding surplus by grid cell |
| 5 | `cwd_surplus_relationship` | all annual slices | Store and plot the CWD-surplus relationship |

The first three jobs are independent. `convert_et_mm` and `simulate_snow` can
then run in parallel. All later jobs are sequential.

The registry can be inspected directly; its resource columns control array
size, concurrency, CPUs, memory, and wall time.

```{bash}
column -t -s $'\t' src/ubelix/jobs.tsv
```

## 4. Submit the whole workflow

The simplest option submits every job, including the final result, with Slurm
`afterok` dependencies:

```{bash}
src/ubelix/submit_pipeline.sh
```

The script submits the three input arrays first. It then builds the dependency
graph shown above. A downstream job becomes eligible only after every required
upstream job or array has completed successfully.

Set cluster-specific controls on the same command when needed. The account
defaults to `gratis`; no partition is requested by default.

```{bash}
MCT_SLURM_ACCOUNT=my_account \
MCT_SLURM_PARTITION=your_partition \
src/ubelix/submit_pipeline.sh
```

If the data paths use an allocated UBELIX Workspace and its environment must be
loaded inside each batch job, add:

```{bash}
MCT_USE_WORKSPACE=1 src/ubelix/submit_pipeline.sh
```

Environment controls can be combined. Export them first when that is easier to
read or when several commands must use the same settings.

## 5. Submit individual work steps

An individual job is submitted by its registry name:

```{bash}
src/ubelix/submit.sh prepare_precipitation
```

To run the workflow checkpoint by checkpoint, submit the independent inputs,
wait until all three have completed successfully, and inspect the status.

```{bash}
src/ubelix/submit.sh prepare_precipitation
src/ubelix/submit.sh prepare_temperature
src/ubelix/submit.sh prepare_et

Rscript analysis/00_status.R
```

Next submit ET conversion and snow simulation. These jobs can run concurrently,
but both must finish before the daily balance is submitted.

```{bash}
src/ubelix/submit.sh convert_et_mm
src/ubelix/submit.sh simulate_snow

src/ubelix/submit.sh calculate_balance
src/ubelix/submit.sh calculate_annual_cwd
src/ubelix/submit.sh cwd_surplus_relationship
```

When using this manual sequence, wait for each dependency wave to finish before
submitting the next one. The submitter does not infer dependencies for a single
job invocation.

An explicit dependency can instead be attached to any individual submission.
For example, after recording the Slurm job ID returned for the annual CWD job:

```{bash}
MCT_DEPENDENCY=afterok:123456 \
src/ubelix/submit.sh cwd_surplus_relationship
```

The final result job can be rerun independently once all annual files exist.
Use `MCT_RESULTS_PER_SLICE` to change the deterministic maximum sample drawn
from each longitude-slice file; the default is 25.

```{bash}
MCT_RESULTS_PER_SLICE=100 \
src/ubelix/submit.sh cwd_surplus_relationship
```

## 6. Monitor jobs and outputs

Use standard Slurm tools to monitor the submitted jobs. The generated job names
start with `mct_` and include the climate run identifier.

```{bash}
squeue --me
sacct -j JOB_ID --format=JobID,JobName%60,State,Elapsed,MaxRSS,ExitCode
```

Standard output and errors are written under `logs/ubelix/`. `%A` in the
submission template becomes the Slurm job ID and `%a` becomes the array task
ID.

```{bash}
ls -lt logs/ubelix
tail -f logs/ubelix/calculate_annual_cwd__*.out
tail -f logs/ubelix/calculate_annual_cwd__*.err
```

Re-run the project status report at any time to compare the number of completed
files with the expected number in the registry.

```{bash}
module load R
Rscript analysis/00_status.R
```

The main tagged checkpoints are:

- configured tidy-cache directories for precipitation, temperature, and ET;
- `data/df_et_mm/df_et_mm_ilon_*.rds`;
- `data/df_snow/df_snow_ilon_*.rds`;
- `data/df_bal/df_bal_ilon_*.rds`;
- `data/df_cwd_annual/df_cwd_annual_ilon_*.rds`;
- `data/cwd_surplus_relationship_sample.rds`;
- `fig/cwd_vs_preceding_surplus.png` and `.pdf`.

Each filename receives the climate run tag, for example
`et-alexi__prec-mswep-v3.16-past__temp-era5-land`, before its extension.

## 7. Restart incomplete work

Longitude-level outputs are written atomically. Existing completed files are
skipped, so the usual recovery procedure is to fix the source of an error and
resubmit the same job:

```{bash}
src/ubelix/submit.sh calculate_annual_cwd
```

Successful longitude files remain in place while missing files are generated.
Do not remove successful checkpoints merely to restart a failed array.

For a targeted recovery, `MCT_ILON` accepts comma-separated indices and closed
ranges. It is exported to every task in the submitted array; tasks without an
assigned selected longitude exit without producing output.

```{bash}
MCT_ILON=3961-3970,5000 \
src/ubelix/submit.sh calculate_annual_cwd
```

Apply the same longitude selection to an upstream step first if its required
checkpoint is also missing. Run `analysis/00_status.R` after recovery before
submitting downstream work.

## 8. Interpret dependency failures

With a full-pipeline submission, an upstream failure prevents dependent jobs
from running. Inspect the failed task's `.err` and `.out` files and its `sacct`
record. After correcting the problem, resubmit the failed stage and then either
submit the remaining stages individually or submit the full workflow again.
Because completed checkpoints are skipped, full resubmission is safe and does
not repeat completed longitude calculations.

The core endpoint is the nested annual data frame produced for every grid cell.
It contains annual maximum CWD and its preceding maximum cumulative surplus.
No extreme-value fitting, return-level analysis, site evaluation, soil or
rooting-depth calculation, or SIF/evaporative-fraction threshold analysis is
submitted by this workflow.
